key_insight: Applying a selective "looping" (repeated reuse) of early-to-middle transformer layers during training for masked diffusion language models (LoopMDM) yields substantial gains in training efficiency and generation quality compared to standard MDM architectures.
problem_solved: Masked diffusion models (MDMs) offer an alternative to autoregressive LMs but lack efficient, well‑designed transformer architectures; training MDMs is compute‑heavy and architectural choices for them are underexplored.
method: Selectively loop (repeatedly apply) early-middle transformer layers during training so the same layer weights process multiple denoising steps, reducing effective model size and compute.
Keep higher layers unlooped to preserve representational capacity and combine looping with the MDM denoising schedule for stable convergence.
Integrate looping into the standard MDM training pipeline to improve throughput and empirical performance without major changes to optimization or loss functions.
impact: LoopMDM reduces compute and memory cost while improving convergence and output quality, making masked diffusion language models more practical to train and scale for researchers and practitioners.
visual_elements: Side-by-side transformer block diagram: standard stack vs looped early-middle layers (arrows showing repeated reuse).
Bar chart comparing training FLOPs/throughput and validation quality (e.g., perplexity or F1) for baseline MDM vs LoopMDM.
Schematic of the masked diffusion denoising schedule annotated with where looping is applied (early/middle layers looped, top layers fixed).
Example text completions or qualitative improvements (baseline vs LoopMDM) to show empirical gains.
paper_authors: Sanghyun Lee, Chunsan Hong, Seungryong Kim, Jonghyun Lee, Jongho Park
